claim_verdicts.evidence: InMemoryEventStore.cs:44 `public EventSourcedOrder Load(int orderId) => EventSourcedOrder.FromEvents(ReadStream(orderId));` with comment "Loading is a replay of the order's whole stream." ReadStream defaults afterVersion = 0.

OrderSnapshots.cs:12 `private readonly Dictionary<int, OrderSnapshot> latest = [];`; :19 `store.Save(order);` first; :21-24 `var snapshotVersion = latest.TryGetValue(order.Id, out var snapshot) ? snapshot.Version : 0; if (order.Version - snapshotVersion >= every) { latest[order.Id] = order.ToSnapshot(); }` — one entry per order id, overwritten.

OrderSnapshots.cs:5 `public sealed record OrderSnapshot(int OrderId, int CustomerId, int TotalVnd, string Status, int Version);` EventSourcedOrder.cs:126 `public OrderSnapshot ToSnapshot() => new(Id, CustomerId, TotalVnd, Status, Version);`

OrderSnapshots.cs:30-39: no snapshot → `var stream = store.ReadStream(orderId); EventsReplayedByLastLoad = stream.Count; return EventSourcedOrder.FromEvents(stream);` else `var eventsAfter = store.ReadStream(orderId, afterVersion: snapshot.Version); EventsReplayedByLastLoad = eventsAfter.Count; return EventSourcedOrder.FromSnapshot(snapshot, eventsAfter);`. Lesson block lines 17-40 matches the source character-for-character.

InMemoryEventStore.cs:32-36 comment "One order's events, oldest first, after the first `afterVersion` of them." and `return stream.Skip(afterVersion).ToList();` (empty list when the stream does not exist).

EventSourcedOrder.cs:128-144 object initializer sets Id, CustomerId, TotalVnd, Status, Version from the snapshot, then `foreach (var domainEvent in eventsAfter) order.Apply(domainEvent);` — same private Apply as FromEvents (:54-63). newEvents is empty, so LoadedVersion (:38 `Version - newEvents.Count`) = snapshot.Version + applied events, which InMemoryEventStore.Save passes to Append as expectedVersion.

InMemoryEventStore.Append :25-26 `if (stream.Count != expectedVersion) throw new StreamConcurrencyException(...)`; OrderSnapshots.Save calls `store.Save(order)` on line 19, before the snapshot check on 21-25, with no try/catch, so the exception leaves Save before any snapshot is written.

OrderSnapshots.cs:42 `public void DeleteAll() => latest.Clear();`; Load's no-snapshot branch (:30-35) reads `store.ReadStream(orderId)` in full. Test asserts `Assert.Equal(3, snapshots.EventsReplayedByLastLoad)` after DeleteAll.

EventSourcingTests.cs:114-132 (lesson block matches verbatim): `new OrderSnapshots(new InMemoryEventStore(), every: 2)`, Place/Save, Pay/Save, Ship/Save; `Assert.Equal(1, ...)` before DeleteAll, `Assert.Equal(3, ...)` after, `Assert.Equal(fromEvents.ToSnapshot(), fromSnapshot.ToSnapshot())`. Traced: versions 1,2,3; 2-0>=2 at save 2 → snapshot v2; 3-2=1<2 at save 3 → none.

"Two variables of a record type are equal if they have the same type, and if, for every field, the values in both records are equal. Classes use reference equality: two variables of a class type are equal if they refer to the same object." Both compared values are OrderSnapshot.

EventSourcedOrder.cs:70 Pay throws `if (Status != "new")`; :76 Cancel throws `if (Status is "cancelled" or "shipped")`; :82 Ship throws `if (Status != "paid")`. Longest sequences through the methods: placed, paid, shipped|cancelled = 3 events.

OrderProjections.cs:12 `public int Position { get; private set; }`; CatchUp iterates `store.ReadAll(Position)` (all streams, append order); Rebuild :23-28 `Clear(); Position = 0; CatchUp(store);`. OrderSnapshot's field is `int Version` (OrderSnapshots.cs:5).

issues.text: Round 3, new in changed s4. I re-read this twice. "no second source" is abstract, and "it" could mean the event or its stored shape. I worked out that new code must still be able to apply events written in the old shape, but only on the second read.
issues.quote: The events have no second source: they keep their stored shape, so new code must still apply it.
issues.fix: Replace with: "The events cannot be taken again from anything else: they keep the shape they were stored with, so new code must still be able to apply events in that old shape."
